# Abstract

The fixture plant is a sterile cultigen grown from its rhizome, and its gingerols turn into shogaols when it is dried [1, 2]. This review is current as of 24 November 2026.

<!-- section: part-i -->
# Part I. Foundations

<!-- section: 1-the-plant -->
## 1. The plant

This opening sentence carries no claim of fact at all, and it only says what the rest of this short section is going to do for the reader. <!-- framing -->

The rhizome is harvested after about ten months in the original study, which grew the plant in a greenhouse under a set regime of light and water [1].

<!-- figure: fig-a -->

Taken together, the two studies describe one plant from two directions. <!-- synthesis -->

<!-- section: 2-the-chemistry -->
## 2. The chemistry

Drying lowered gingerol content and raised shogaol content in the second study [2], which a later meta-analysis did not revisit [2].
